title: Successor step in the right external cup coefficient bound
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X,Y$ quasi-compact $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine diagonals, and $F,G$ quasi-coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Use the scalar resolution models [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-resolution-model] and normalization [lem-sc-picard-external-cup-cochain]. Write $H^p$ for module right-derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Fix $F$ and $d\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that for every quasi-coherent $G\prime$ with $H^p(Y,G\prime)=0$ whenever $d<p$, every normalized realization has invertible homology in every natural degree. If $H^p(Y,G)=0$ whenever $d+1<p$, then every normalized realization for $(F,G)$ has invertible homology in every natural degree.

source.place: Varieties Tag 0BED proof after equation 33.29.1.1: exact coefficient sequences, two dimension-shifting inductions and acyclic Leray base case

proof.text:
For the coefficient being shifted, equip the scheme with its given k-structure, embed the module in an acyclic quasi-coherent E, and take the quasi-coherent cokernel Q. The long exact module cohomology sequence identifies H^p(Q) with H^(p+1) of the original module for p>0. For d

0 and d+1

Choose finite affine covers and the product cover. Sections on affine intersections are exact on quasi-coherent modules; the section pullback and tensor formulas identify product sections with tensors of factor sections. Field tensor is exact. Hence the signed refinement/cup comparisons form a map of short exact sequences of complexes, in the coefficient being shifted. The affine Cech comparisons and their naturality identify the long exact homology ladder with the external cup comparison, including connecting maps.

Take normalized realizations for E and Q from the cochain existence theorem and apply the supplied bound-d induction hypothesis to both in every natural degree. Tensor Kunneth cycle spanning and normalization identify their homology maps with the transported Cech comparisons. The five lemma makes the comparison for the original coefficient invertible. The same spanning and normalization argument identifies any specified c with that comparison, so H(c) is invertible. This proves exactly one successor step and does not assume the conclusion for unbounded coefficients.

lean.statement:
theorem picardExternalCupCochain_isIso_shiftRight
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [CompactSpace Y]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal g)]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (d : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (G' : Y.Modules) [G'.IsQuasicoherent],
      (∀ p : ℕ, d < p →
        IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p).obj G')) →
      ∀ (c' : picardExternalTotal f g F G' ⟶
        picardScalarModel (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G')),
        IsPicardExternalCupCochain f g F G' c' → ∀ n : ℕ,
          IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c' (n : ℤ)))
    (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hG : ∀ p : ℕ, d + 1 < p →
      IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p).obj G))
    (c : picardExternalTotal f g F G ⟶
      picardScalarModel (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))
    (hc : IsPicardExternalCupCochain f g F G c) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap c (n : ℤ))
